description: Words, phrases, n-grams, constructions and POS templates reported as over-represented (or, where marked, under-represented) in LLM-generated or LLM-assisted text. Every item was string-matched against the full text of its source (or, for Matsui 2025, the Crossref abstract). Statistics are copied from the sources; null means the source gives no item-level number.
usage_notes: Register matters: Reinhart et al. stress that many of these words are normal in fiction but conspicuous in academic, news or spoken registers. Flag by register, do not ban globally.
Kobak, Juzek & Ward, Gray, Matsui and Geng & Trotta measure shifts in published human-authored scholarly text (LLM-assisted), not raw LLM output.
Antislop trigrams are stopword-removed; match them after stopword removal or as skip-grams.
Replacing listed words is a surface operation; studies in humanization_research.md show it does not move structural/narrative or style-embedding signals.

Kobak2025.cite: Kobak, González-Márquez, Horvát, Lause (2025). Delving into LLM-assisted writing in biomedical publications through excess vocabulary. Science Advances 11(27).
Kobak2025.corpus: PubMed abstracts 2010-2024 (excess usage vs counterfactual extrapolation)
Kobak2025.caveat: Excess words in published (LLM-assisted) human abstracts, not raw LLM output. Rare set has frequency < 0.02 by construction.

JuzekWard2025.cite: Juzek & Ward (2025). Why Does ChatGPT "Delve" So Much? Exploring the Sources of Lexical Overrepresentation in Large Language Models. COLING 2025.

LiangICML2024.cite: Liang et al. (2024). Monitoring AI-Modified Content at Scale: A Case Study on the Impact of ChatGPT on AI Conference Peer Reviews. ICML 2024 (PMLR 235).
LiangICML2024.corpus: ICLR/NeurIPS/CoRL/EMNLP peer reviews; AI vs human reviews
LiangICML2024.caveat: Lists ranked by disproportionate AI usage; individual ratios given only for three adjectives.

Liang2024Mapping.cite: Liang et al. (2024). Mapping the Increasing Use of LLMs in Scientific Papers.
Liang2024Mapping.venue: UNVERIFIED (arXiv preprint verified; publication venue not confirmed by lookup)

Reinhart2025.cite: Reinhart, Markey, Laudenbach, Pantusen, Yurko, Weinberg, Brown (2025). Do LLMs write like humans? Variation in grammatical and rhetorical styles. PNAS 122, e2422455122.
Reinhart2025.corpus: HAP-E parallel corpus (6 genres) and CAP (COCA registers)
Reinhart2025.caveat: Table 1 base-model columns (proper names, artefacts) excluded; only instruction-tuned columns kept.

Paech2025Antislop.cite: Paech et al. (2025). Antislop: A Comprehensive Framework for Identifying and Eliminating Repetitive Patterns in Language Models.
Paech2025Antislop.corpus: creative-writing outputs of 67 models vs human baseline (wordfreq + Reddit creative writing + Project Gutenberg)
Paech2025Antislop.caveat: Trigrams are stopword-removed (e.g. 'voice barely whisper' = 'voice barely above a whisper').

Gray2024.cite: Gray (2024). ChatGPT "contamination": estimating the prevalence of LLMs in the scholarly literature.

GengTrotta2024.cite: Geng & Trotta (2024). Is ChatGPT Transforming Academics' Writing Style?

Chakrabarty2025LAMP.cite: Chakrabarty, Laban, Wu (2025). Can AI writing be salvaged? Mitigating Idiosyncrasies and Improving Human-AI Alignment in the Writing Process through Edits. CHI 2025.

Chakrabarty2024TTCW.cite: Chakrabarty, Laban, Agarwal, Muresan, Wu (2024). Art or Artifice? Large Language Models and the False Promise of Creativity. CHI 2024.

Herbold2023.cite: Herbold, Hautli-Janisz, Heuer, Kikteva, Trautsch (2023). A large-scale comparison of human-written versus new ChatGPT-generated essays.
Herbold2023.venue: UNVERIFIED (journal version not confirmed by lookup)

Matsui2025.cite: Matsui (2025). Delving Into PubMed Records: How AI-Influenced Vocabulary has Transformed Medical Writing since ChatGPT. Perspectives on Medical Education.
Matsui2025.caveat: Only the five terms named in the abstract are included (full 135-term list not retrieved).
